The most likely corrupted element is **Cc**. At 12.2 fF it is far too small for a 2 pF load: the simulated UGBW (42 MHz) sits above the output pole gm7/CL (about 29 MHz), which drives PM to -11.55°. Its +20% sensitivity is positive, so more Cc helps PM, consistent with an undersized value. A units slip (1.219e-12 intended) is a plausible cause.

I ruled out the matched pairs. M1/M2 and M3/M4 have identical sizing and matching bias currents, and the offset (-0.43 mV) is small, so a single fault in either pair is unlikely. M5, M6, and M8 are consistent with the 10 µA reference through their mirror ratios.

The Miller compensation is undersized, so UGBW (~42 MHz) lands above the output pole gm7/CL (~29 MHz) and PM collapses to -11.55 deg. Restoring Cc to the correct scale should recover PM. M7 (L=0.272 um, unusually short for the output device) is the second candidate, and M3/M4 the third."}
